thread:
marta: quick question — we've seen a couple incidents where SDK clients land with Authorization present but X-Project-Id is missing (proxy strip / old SDK). Current behavior seems to silently fallback to org default project and charge the org. Is that intended?

devon: intended originally for compatibility with old clients, but we never instrumented telemetry to see how often fallback happens. can we decide: strict reject vs graceful fallback + telemetry?

samir: leaning toward a two-phase plan: 1) log telemetry + warning header for 2 weeks, 2) canary enforce reject for a small % of traffic, 3) full reject. We need clear error shapes so SDKs can auto-detect and prompt users.

marta: agree. proposed error mapping (suggestion):
- No Authorization header => 401 + body {"error":"missing_auth"}
- Authorization invalid/unknown => 401 + {"error":"invalid_api_key"}
- Key expired => 401 + {"error":"key_expired","expires_at":"<iso>"}
- Key valid but X-Project-Id missing AND key is project-scoped => 400 + {"error":"missing_project_header"} (client fix)
- Key valid but project mismatch (X-Project-Id set but not allowed) => 403 + {"error":"project_forbidden"}
- Key org-scoped and X-Project-Id missing => (phase 1) 200 but include response header X-Auth-Fallback: org-default and telemetry flag; (phase 2) 400/403?

nadeem: fwiw, customers strongly dislike silent re-attribution. If fallback causes billing surprises, support tickets blow up. I vote to emit a warning header and metric immediately, and start canary rejects after 7 days.

devon: ok timeline sounds fine. concrete telemetry we should add: metric auth.fallback_used{org,route,client_sdk_version}, and a new response header: X-Auth-Feedback: fallback|rejected|ok; also include X-Auth-Fallback-Reason when fallback applied.

samir: add SDK behavior notes: SDKs should detect 400/403 with error codes above and surface a clear message: "Missing Project ID — update SDK or set X-Project-Id header". We can ship a patch to the JS and Python SDKs to log a diagnostic and optionally auto-pop a migration guide link.

marta: example incoming header expectations for docs and test harness:
```
Authorization: Bearer rk-abc123
X-Org-Id: org_redwood
X-Project-Id: proj_customerA  # optional for org-scoped keys only during grace window
User-Agent: redwood-sdk-js/1.2.3
```

marta: also propose response snippet for missing project during canary (reject):
```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json
X-Auth-Feedback: rejected
{
  "error": "missing_project_header",
  "message": "Requests with project-scoped API keys must include X-Project-Id. See https://redwood.ai/docs/auth for migration steps."
}
```

devon: question: should proxies that strip headers be considered a special case? e.g., GCP load balancers often strip custom headers unless configured. We should include a diagnostic header like X-Auth-Diagnostic that SDKs can log to help customers and SEs.

samir: yes — include X-Auth-Diagnostic: proxy-strip-detected when we see org header but not project but client reported SDK version < 1.3.0 (heuristic). Not perfect but useful.

marta: rollout plan (concrete):
1) PR to runtime: add telemetry + X-Auth-Feedback + X-Auth-Fallback-Reason (today) — low-risk, ship to prod.
2) Enable telemetry dashboards and alert if fallback rate > 0.1% per org.
3) After 7 days, create canary that returns 400 for 1% of orgs (random) when fallback would be used. Monitor false positive and support noise.
4) If tolerable, increase to full enforcement after 14 days.

nadeem: support/ops note: add a canned support response template for billing chargebacks if fallback caused mis-attribution. Link to audit logs we will surface (auth.fallback_count).

devon: I'll open the runtime PR for header instrumentation and telemetry. @marta can you own the SDK behavior changes (JS + Py) and docs update? @samir can you write the error spec in the API contract doc and add tests for all shapes?

marta: yes, will do. will also add migration note with code snippet for setting X-Project-Id in browser SDK.

samir: pinging for reviews: @devon please include the new response headers in the gateway contract. I'll draft the API spec change and unit tests.

infra-bot: canary gate created for auth-fallback-enforce (1% traffic) — ID cg-87321. Will notify when deployed to canary. :robot_face:

marta: thanks — one last thing: let's standardize on header names: X-Project-Id, X-Org-Id, Authorization. avoid X-Project for legacy shorthands. I'll add a lint rule in the SDKs to normalize header casing.

devon: perfect. I'll link the PRs in this thread as they land. TL;DR: telemetry now -> canary rejects in 7 days -> full enforcement after successful canary.

marta: thanks all — assigning action items in linear after lunch. :thumbsup:
